error.cannot_connect: Unable to connect to AiDot servers.

data.sdes_fast_liveplay: SDES fast connect (faster signaling, on by default)

data_description.serve_port_base: Base local port for serving SDES camera streams to HA/go2rtc (each camera uses base..base+399). Change only if it conflicts with another service.
data_description.connection_mode: How cameras connect. Automatic (recommended) offers every path and prefers the LAN, keeping the cloud relay as a fallback - cameras on the same LAN connect directly, and only a camera with no direct route rides the relay. LAN only skips the relay for a faster (~1s vs ~3-4s) start, but a camera that cannot reach Home Assistant directly will not connect (battery cameras keep the relay regardless - it is their only path back from a cloud wake). Each camera reports the path in use under Diagnostics as media_path.
data_description.sdes_fast_liveplay: Matches the official app: skip the livePlayResp wait and go straight to the video handshake, so SDES (battery) cameras start ~4.5 s sooner. ON by default. The PTZ camera is automatically excluded (its handshake needs the slower path). If you ever see a live view drop to a snapshot on a specific camera, turn this off.
data_description.mains_idle_s: How long to keep a mains-powered camera's live session warm after the last viewer, so re-opening it is instant instead of paying the full cold-start handshake. Default 0 = never release (always warm, instant views). Set a positive window (e.g. 300 = 5 min) to let unwatched cameras go dormant; a dormant camera reconnects on view in roughly 15-22s. Each warm camera keeps decrypting, which costs host CPU. Battery cameras ignore this (they warm on motion to save battery).
data_description.enable_local_control: Route camera settings (LED, motion detection, night vision, sensitivity, volume, PTZ tracking) over the LAN instead of the cloud, for eligible mains-powered cameras. Faster and works during cloud outages; falls back to cloud automatically. Does not affect video. Battery cameras are skipped.
data_description.startup_prewarm: Open a session on every mains camera in the background at startup (staggered), so the first live view after a restart is instant instead of paying the 15-20s cold start. On by default; turn off to save host CPU when views are rare. Battery cameras are excluded.
data_description.sdes_pin_h264: Stops a camera from switching itself to H.265 mid-session. Some cameras ignore the requested codec and answer with H.265 at a much larger frame size; players that use Media Source Extensions (the Home Assistant iOS app among them) may then show only about one frame per keyframe. Turn this on if live view is very choppy on one camera but fine on others. Off by default: a camera that can only encode H.265 would have nothing to send.

data_description.sdes_audio: Include audio in SDES (battery) camera streams, matching the official app. On by default: the stream feeds the audio encoder a continuous silence base so audio from battery cameras plays smoothly. Turn off only if you don't want camera audio.
data_description.sdes_audio_gain_db: Volume trim for camera audio. The camera microphone runs hot, so the default (-8 dB) tames it. Raise toward 0 (or positive) if audio is too quiet; lower if it clips. Applies to SDES (battery) cameras.
data_description.hls_audio: Also publish an AAC copy of each camera's audio, encoded in-process, so Home Assistant's own HLS dialog (the Picture cards) and camera.record recordings have sound; WebRTC views already carry the camera's audio. Applies to cameras that publish directly: every SDES camera, and standard cameras with Direct publish on. Costs about 2-3% of one CPU core per streaming camera. Turn it off to save that, or if a camera's HLS audio misbehaves. On by default.
data_description.hls_direct_ts: Home Assistant's HLS dialog and recordings read the camera's stream straight from this integration, with sound and picture on one clock, instead of through go2rtc. Through go2rtc, a recording that starts while the camera is already streaming can have its sound up to about 0.75 s behind the picture. Live WebRTC views are unchanged. Needs 'Direct publish into go2rtc' and 'Audio in HLS and recordings' on. SDES cameras (the battery and PTZ models) take part too: turning this on also pins their video to H.264, as 'Pin camera video to H.264' does, because a session that answers in H.265 cannot feed this stream. Off by default while it is being validated.
data_description.direct_publish: Publish each camera's video and audio straight into go2rtc without an ffmpeg process in between, and do it for every camera model (DTLS cameras stop using a local serve port). Fewer moving parts. Live WebRTC views carry the camera's own audio, untranscoded. Home Assistant's own HLS dialog and recordings get the camera's audio through 'Audio in HLS and recordings'. Off by default while it is being validated.

data.title: Notification title
data.open_in_app: Open the clip inside the Home Assistant app (experimental)

data_description.targets: The notify services to send to (for example a phone running the companion app). Used by every camera that does not set its own targets. You can type a service name that is not listed.
data_description.cooldown_s: After a notification for a camera, further motion from that camera is not sent for this long. A person detection still gets through a cooldown that plain motion started. 0 disables the cooldown.
data_description.title: Placeholders: camera, event (motion/person), event_title (Motion/Person), time, device_id. Write each one inside curly braces in the title or message.
data_description.open_in_app: When a notification is tapped, play the event's clip on a page inside the Home Assistant app. Off: the tap opens the clip's own link, which the iPhone app opens in Safari.

data_description.camera: The camera whose notification settings to change.

data_description.events: Off: never. All: every motion and person event. Person only: only when the camera reports a person.
data_description.targets: Leave empty to use the default targets.

abort.no_cameras: No cameras are loaded yet. Try again once the integration has finished starting.

talk_no_audio.message: No audio could be decoded from {media} - check the media URL or path.

talk_session_failed.message: Could not establish a talk session (camera must be streaming - open the live view first).

ptz_failed.message: PTZ command {direction} was not sent (camera must be streaming - open the live view first).

command_rejected.message: AiDot {action} was rejected by the device.

go2rtc_rejects_stream_updates.title: go2rtc rejects stream updates
go2rtc_rejects_stream_updates.description: go2rtc answered the registration of stream `{stream}` with an error, and the stream was still there. Its configuration file (go2rtc.yaml) most likely holds a stream listed twice, which makes go2rtc reject every registration for every camera until the duplicate is removed by hand. Live view keeps working from what go2rtc already holds; a camera added or renamed since will not register. See the troubleshooting section of the README. This message goes away once a registration succeeds.
